articles.title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect: Practice Questions
articles.lead: Hands-on questions, exam strategy, FAQs, and resources.
articles.body_html:
7-Day Study Plan

  1. Core services: IAM, VPC, EC2, S3, CloudFront
  2. Databases: RDS/Aurora/DynamoDB, backups, DR basics
  3. Compute patterns: Lambda, ECS/EKS, autoscaling
  4. Networking: endpoints, VPN/Direct Connect, routing
  5. Security: KMS, policies, logging
  6. Resilience: Multi-AZ vs Multi-Region, RTO/RPO
  7. Full practice set + review weak domains

Practice Questions (sample)

Q1. Best way to serve a static website globally with lowest latency?
A: S3 + CloudFront + Route 53, with origin access control.

Q2. Need automatic scaling for spiky background jobs?
A: SQS + Lambda event source mapping.

Q3. Shared filesystem across many EC2 across AZs?
A: EFS.

FAQs

How do I review wrong answers? Write why each wrong option violates requirements (latency, availability, cost, security).

How many questions per day? Start 15–25 mixed questions/day, then increase once accuracy stabilizes.

Resources

  • AWS Well-Architected Framework
  • SAA-C03 Exam Guide
  • AWS Documentation

articles.title: Cybersecurity CEH: Hands-on Labs
articles.lead: Recon, exploitation basics, and defensive validation with safe lab practice.
articles.body_html:
Step-by-step Lab Path

  1. Set up a safe lab (VMs + isolated network)
  2. Recon: DNS, ports, service fingerprinting
  3. Web testing basics: auth, input validation, sessions
  4. Exploit fundamentals in labs only (no real targets)
  5. Privilege escalation patterns (Linux/Windows)
  6. Logging + detection: validate what defenders see
  7. Report writing: findings, impact, remediation

Practice Tasks

Run a scan against a lab target, list services, and map each service to an attack surface. Then write mitigations (patch, config, WAF, segmentation).

FAQs

Do I need paid tools? No. Start with free lab tooling and focus on methodology and reporting.

How to stay compliant? Use only owned/lab targets; keep written authorization for any testing outside your lab.

Resources

  • OWASP Top 10
  • MITRE ATT&CK
  • Kali Linux

articles.title: ITIL 4 Foundation: Key Concepts
articles.lead: Service value system, practices, and vocabulary you must know.
articles.body_html:
7-Day Study Plan

  1. SVS + guiding principles
  2. Value chain activities
  3. Practices overview (what/why)
  4. Continual improvement model
  5. Service relationships + value streams
  6. Mock questions + glossary review
  7. Final mixed set + weak areas

FAQs

How to avoid rote memorization? Map each concept to a real workplace example.

articles.title: PMP: Fast Track
articles.lead: Processes, artifacts, and exam strategy focused on scenario questions.
articles.body_html:
Fast Track Workflow

  1. Read the ECO and map domains to your weak areas
  2. Study agile + hybrid patterns first
  3. Do 20–30 scenario questions/day
  4. Review explanations; build a mistake log
  5. Full mock weekly; fix weakest domain

FAQs

What matters most on exam day? Scenario reasoning and choosing the next best action.

articles.title: Best Exam Dumps Alternatives
articles.lead: Ethical, reliable ways to study with higher retention and less risk.
articles.body_html:
Safer Alternatives

  • Official exam guides + blueprint-based study plan
  • Practice tests from reputable providers
  • Hands-on labs/projects that match objectives
  • Error log + spaced repetition flashcards

FAQs

Why avoid dumps? They risk disqualification and usually reduce real skill retention.
